issues.description: Command names (quickmarks-reload/bookmarks-reload) violate the singular noun-verb convention used by sibling commands.
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-load (singular). The new commands introduce plural-noun-verb naming in the same namespace without justification. Align with the existing convention: quickmark-reload and bookmark-reload.

issues.description: reload() is not atomic: a parse failure leaves marks empty rather than preserving prior state.
issues.detail: reload() calls self.marks.clear() then re-parses. If _init_lineparser or _parse_line raises, marks is left empty while the on-disk file is intact, and the changed signal state is incoherent. Build the new OrderedDict in a local, then swap atomically and emit once on success.

issues.description: Constructor postcondition silently changed: reload() now emits changed during __init__.
issues.detail: Routing initialisation through reload() causes changed to fire from the constructor, before _init_savemanager runs and before observers can connect. Combined with the save-manager wiring, this also risks a reload-triggered autosave round-trip. Either suppress the signal during construction or explicitly document the new behavior.

issues.description: Tests assert only the info message, not that marks were actually replaced from disk.
issues.detail: The new BDD scenarios are unnamed and only check that an info string appeared. They do not mutate the file on disk and assert the resulting marks, and no unit test covers the QuickmarkManager path. Name the scenarios, exercise both managers, and assert the post-reload contents.

issues.description: changed signal fires on every reload even when contents are identical.
issues.detail: reload() unconditionally emits changed, causing subscribers to re-render or re-save needlessly. A cheap dict comparison would let the emit be skipped when the new value equals the old, avoiding spurious downstream work and an unnecessary autosave.

issues.description: Parse loop duplicated/conflated with reload; extract a pure parse helper.
issues.detail: The parse loop still mutates self.marks in place. Extract a pure helper that takes lines and returns a dict, so reload becomes: read, parse-to-value, swap, emit. This separates value computation from identity mutation and supports the atomic-swap fix above.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a small, well-scoped refactor exposing reload as a command, but it ships half-finished. The two unanimous P1s are command naming (plural breaks the singular sibling convention) and non-atomic reload (clear-then-parse leaves marks empty on failure). A further P1 concern is that routing __init__ through reload silently changes the constructor's signal contract and risks an autosave round-trip. Tests verify the info-message string rather than the actual reload behavior, and the QuickmarkManager path is untested. Verdict: salvageable with one more pass to align names, build-then-swap, and test the real behavior.
